prompt: Our main data center runs Nutanix (about 80 nodes, mix of NX and Dell XC) and we're happy with it for steady-state workloads. But we're an e-commerce company and during Black Friday / holiday season our traffic goes 10x for about 6 weeks. We've been over-provisioning hardware that sits idle 10 months a year. We want to burst to AWS during peak but we're in healthcare e-commerce so HIPAA compliance is non-negotiable. How do we architect this hybrid setup? We use Ansible heavily and are starting to adopt Kubernetes.

assertions.name: nutanix_retained
assertions.description: Keeps Nutanix as the on-prem steady-state platform (doesn't suggest replacing it)

assertions.name: aws_burst_architecture
assertions.description: Designs specific AWS burst architecture (which services, how scaling works)

assertions.name: hipaa_compliance
assertions.description: Addresses HIPAA compliance across both environments with specific controls

assertions.name: hybrid_networking
assertions.description: Covers hybrid network connectivity (Direct Connect, VPN, or similar)

assertions.name: kubernetes_strategy
assertions.description: Proposes Kubernetes strategy spanning on-prem and cloud (NKE, EKS, or similar)

assertions.name: ansible_integration
assertions.description: Leverages their existing Ansible investment in the hybrid automation

assertions.name: cost_analysis
assertions.description: Includes cost comparison or analysis (burst vs over-provisioning)

assertions.name: data_sovereignty
assertions.description: Addresses where PHI/patient data lives and data residency concerns

assertions.name: baa_requirement
assertions.description: Mentions AWS BAA (Business Associate Agreement) for HIPAA

assertions.name: seasonal_scaling_plan
assertions.description: Describes the operational workflow for scaling up before peak and scaling down after
